_comment: S87-T-007 Figure 4 failure shape — controlled comparison with requires_exact_data_match and numeric must_show pairs. Reconstructed from live DP affordance va-S5-base-rate-comparison-01 (genericised labels only where needed for fixture clarity; values and relationships match the live defect).

visual_affordance.rationale: The conceptual point depends on changing only the prior while holding test characteristics fixed.
visual_affordance.subject: Comparison of 1% and 20% prevalence scenarios with identical test characteristics.
visual_affordance.context: Place after the section comparison to consolidate how changing prevalence alters the posterior.
visual_affordance.reasoning_supported: Learners isolate the prior as the changing quantity and compare its effect on posterior probability while recognising that the evidence model remains constant.
visual_affordance.canonical_discipline_note: Hold the 90% positive rate with the condition and 5% positive rate without the condition constant across both scenarios.
must_show: 1% prevalence leading to a posterior of about 15.4%
20% prevalence leading to a posterior of about 81.8%
90% positive rate among people with the condition in both scenarios
5% positive rate among people without the condition in both scenarios
A clear indication that prevalence is the quantity that changes
must_not_show: Different test characteristics between the two scenarios
An implication that the test becomes more accurate when prevalence rises
allowed_claims: The same test characteristics can yield different posterior probabilities when the prior changes.
The prior contributes to the interpretation of the evidence.
disallowed_claims: Higher prevalence makes the test itself more accurate.
visual_affordance.source_basis: Controlled prevalence comparison with matched evidence characteristics.
visual_affordance.caption_intent: Changing the prior from 1% to 20% changes the posterior even though the test characteristics remain fixed.
visual_affordance.alt_text: Matched comparison showing identical 90% and 5% test rates with prevalence changing from 1% to 20%, producing posterior probabilities of about 15.4% and 81.8%.
visual_affordance.detailed_description: Two parallel scenarios use identical test characteristics. The first begins with 1% prevalence and ends with a posterior of about 15.4%. The second begins with 20% prevalence and ends with a posterior of about 81.8%. Shared annotations make clear that the test rates are held constant while prevalence changes.
